priceSnapshot.note: THE MAGNET WAS TAGGED, IT HELD BY FIVE DOLLARS, AND THE MARKET BOUNCED 2.4% OFF IT. That is the whole day. Yesterday's morning report named 62,279.54 as the heaviest single feature on the 48h liquidation map and parked the second reduce notch there, noting it had NEVER been tagged in this leg. It was tagged at 13:30 COT on 1 August: the low printed 62,284.3, four dollars and ninety cents above the band, and not one 4H candle closed beneath it. From that low price has travelled to 63,782.4 - a 2.40% recovery - and the 4H EMA200 at 63,263.29, the exact line the last report named as its add trigger, has been reclaimed and closed above twice (63,451.4 and 63,570.6). The failed break is now a failed flush as well. What tempers this is that it happened on a Sunday with the daily structure still broken: price remains under the daily EMA20 at 63,955.52, the daily MACD histogram is still deeply negative at -204.66, and Fear and Greed sits at 28. Session range measured from the 2026-08-01 10:25 COT wallet snapshot is 62,284.3 - 63,782.4.

overnightRisk: THE GAP THAT MATTERS IS THE SUNDAY-NIGHT TO MONDAY-MORNING HANDOFF, AND THIS ONE HAS A SPECIFIC SHAPE. The next report is roughly six and a half hours away at 02:00 COT, but the real event is the Asian equity open and then the US Monday session, and three things sit in the way. FIRST, the entire 2.40% recovery from 62,284.3 happened across a weekend on a positioning flip that is now spent - Long/Short normalised from 42.93/57.07 to 49.48/50.52, so the short base that mechanically fuelled this bounce has largely covered. Weekend rallies built on covering rather than on new bid routinely give back on the Monday open when real size returns. SECOND, the ETF tape is a known negative that has not yet been allowed to act on price: Farside published 31 July at MINUS $265.4M, the largest single-day outflow since 24 July, led by IBIT -122.7 and FBTC -54.8, and because 1 and 2 August were a weekend there has been no new print to either confirm or reverse it. Monday's creation window is the first chance for that flow to express itself, and if the outflow continues it lands on a market that has already used up its short-covering fuel. THIRD, the structural picture underneath is still broken - price is beneath the daily EMA20 (63,955.52), EMA50 (64,855.01), EMA100 (67,263.97) and EMA200 (72,089.79), and the daily MACD histogram is -204.66. Nothing about today changed the daily trend; it changed the intraday one. The concrete risk is a Monday-open fade through 63,000.0, which was the 2 August COT-day low to the dollar and is now the shelf the whole reclaim rests on. Below it there is verified liquidation weight near 63,020 and then a genuine air pocket down to the 62,284.3 low, which is why the resting stop at 62,940 is recommended rather than optional. The upside version of the same risk is a Monday gap through the 63,915.95 magnet, where 621.54K of leverage sits 0.90% above spot - that is the closest large pool on the map and the market has spent the whole session drifting toward it.

atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC over 47 sessions through the in-progress 2026-08-03 UTC candle, seeded on a 14-bar simple average of true range then Wilder-smoothed. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), then ATR = (ATRprev x 13 + TR) / 14. ATR has CONTRACTED again from the 2026-08-01 reading of 1,618.76 to 1,508.22 (-6.8%), a second consecutive contraction, because the completed 2026-08-02 daily candle covered 63,782.4 - 62,809.3 = $973 against a 14-day average of $1,508. At 2.38% of spot a normal day covers about $1,508; the 62,284.3-to-63,782.4 recovery was $1,498, which is almost exactly one ATR - the bounce was a full day's range delivered in under thirty hours. This also frames the recommended 62,940 stop: it is 407 points from spot, or 0.27 ATR, which is tight in absolute terms but is 42% of the entire realised range of the completed 2 August candle.

calibration.rollingRecord: Yesterday's morning report called range with a bullish tilt at 33/42/25 and opened a small 3x futures long at 63,106.0 with a 62,690 stop. The DIRECTION was right and the EXECUTION was wrong. Price fell to 62,284.3 within three hours, took the stop out at 62,690 at 12:45 COT, and then rallied 2.40% to 63,782.4 - the trade was correct and the desk was not in it. The second reduce level at 62,279.54 did NOT fire; the low stopped 4.90 points above it and no 4H candle closed below, which is the single best call in the last week of reports. The 63,269.18 add level DID fire, on two consecutive 4H closes at 63,451.4 and 63,570.6. Scored strictly: the bias was right, the reduce level was right, the add level was right, and acting through a 416-point stop against a 1,619-point ATR turned a winning read into a small loss. That is the third consecutive session where the desk's level work has been better than its position sizing.
calibration.note: The lesson is not directional, it is about stop distance relative to volatility. A 416-point stop is 0.26 of a daily ATR. On an asset that routinely covers a full ATR in a session, a stop that tight is a coin flip on noise, and here it lost the flip by 405 points before the thesis paid 676. Today's report responds concretely: it takes ZERO futures exposure into the overnight gap and expresses the same bullish tilt through spot, where there is no stop to be hunted and no liquidation price. The one leveraged lesson the desk should keep is that its LEVEL identification is working - 62,279.54 was named as untagged and it was tagged to within five dollars and held, which is as precise as this kind of analysis gets.
